PI3K-activated AMPA receptor Glur2 complex was formed within 1 day post ischemia and this complex was responsible for the long term neuroprotective effect of propofol in ischemic stroke.
propofol induced PI3K-α-AMPA receptor complex formation and stabilized the structure of AMPA receptor in the postsynapse, which resulted in the long-term neuroprotection.

the PI3K-mediated acute post-conditioning neuroprotective effect of propofol was associated with the inhibition of internalization of the AMPA receptor Glur2 subunit, and that this neuroprotection was sustained for 28 days.

the early stage formation of PI3k-AMPA receptor subunit complex, which facilitates the long term neuroprotective effects of propofol.
the early stage formation of PI3k-AMPA receptor complex and its long term effects on the post-ischemic neuroprotection.
the early stage of PI3K mediated post-conditioning neuroprotective signaling and provides new insights for the development of PI3K based therapeutic strategies for ischemic stroke.

the formation of PI3-AMPAR Glur2 subunit complex in the early stage of post-conditioning is a critical mechanism for propofol post-ischemic neuroprotection.
the early stage formation of PI3-AMPAR Glur2 complex facilitated the long term neuroprotective effect of propofol in rats.

PI3K- AMPA receptor Glur2 subunit complex is a novel signaling pathway that mediates the long term neuroprotective effect induced by propofl post-conditioning.
PI3K activation by propofol in the early stage after ischemic injury is essential for the long term neuroprotective effect induced by propofal post-conditioning.

PI3K- AMPAR GluR 2 subunit complex is a critical target for the long term neuroprotective effect of propofol.
